title: When the Wolf Breaks
premise: Ansel Okonkwo, the last oath-bound swordspeaker, keeps ledgers for a guild that trades in impossible things — debts of memory, years, and names. When the old gods begin answering prayers again, each answered prayer burns dragon-fire from the world's last hearth, and Ansel discovers his own guild brokered the bargain that bound a king to the god wearing his crown. To save both king and world, Ansel must break his sacred oath and speak the unbinding — an act that will erase every memory anyone holds of him. He does so, unbinding the king and extinguishing the gods' hunger, but chooses love over survival: the woman who remembers him against all law keeps his name alive in a single ledger line, and through her he begins, faintly, to return.
about_author: Astrid Yarrow is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing guild records in coastal trading cities before turning to fiction. She writes about oaths, ledgers, and the people history forgets on purpose.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Ansel Okonkwo audits the Guild of Impossible Things' ledgers, revealing how memory is bought and sold. A desperate widow trades her dead husband's name for bread. Ansel's POV establishes his dry precision and buried grief; the emotional beat is quiet loneliness beneath competence.

chapters.title: A Prayer Answered in Ash
chapters.summary: In the fishing quarter, a drowned child walks out of the sea alive — and the harbor's ancient beacon-stone goes cold. Ansel investigates as guild auditor, finding scorched prayer-marks. His POV; the beat is dread: miracles have a price, and someone is paying it.

chapters.title: The Ledger That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Ansel finds a sealed ledger predating the guild itself, written in his own oath-script, recording a contract between a dying god and a king. Master Veyra orders it burned. Ansel's POV; the beat is betrayal — his institution knew, and hid it.

chapters.title: Sera of the Ninth Bell
chapters.summary: Sera Iln, a bell-keeper who hears which gods are listening, confronts Ansel about the cold beacon. Their sharp exchange becomes reluctant alliance. Alternating POV begins; the beat is wary attraction between two people who trust nothing.

chapters.title: What the Crown Remembers
chapters.summary: Ansel gains audience with King Aldric and realizes the man on the throne flickers — sometimes young, sometimes hollow-eyed and ancient. The god wearing the crown speaks through him briefly. Ansel's POV; the beat is horror wrapped in pity.

chapters.title: Dragon-Fire Guttering
chapters.summary: Sera leads Ansel to the Last Hearth, the sleeping dragon whose fire fuels all old magic. It is dimming with every answered prayer. The dragon, half-dreaming, names Ansel 'the one who signed.' Sera's POV; the beat is awe curdling into urgency.

chapters.title: Terms of the Old Contract
chapters.summary: Deciphering the ancient ledger, Ansel learns the binding: the king traded his name to a starving god for his kingdom's survival, and only a swordspeaker's unbinding can undo it — at the cost of the speaker's own name. Ansel's POV; the beat is grim arithmetic.

chapters.title: The Guild Calls In Its Oath
chapters.summary: Master Veyra invokes Ansel's oath: he must protect the guild's secrets above all, including the contract. Refusal means excommunication and the loss of his speaking-gift. Ansel's POV; the beat is duty tightening like a noose.

chapters.title: Nights in the Bell Tower
chapters.summary: While the city prays and the dragon dims, Ansel and Sera map which gods answer and where. Between work, something tender and unspoken grows. Sera's POV; the beat is warmth stolen from a collapsing world.

chapters.title: Miracle Riots
chapters.summary: Answered prayers spark frenzy: the healed, the returned, the resurrected crowd the temples while whole districts go magically dark. Ansel saves Sera from a mob worshipping the crowned god. Dual POV; the beat is love declared mid-crisis.

chapters.title: Veyra's Confession
chapters.summary: Master Veyra reveals she was the guild clerk who witnessed the original binding — and that she has been feeding prayers to the god to keep it asleep, spending her own memories. Ansel's POV; the beat is compassion for an enemy.

chapters.title: The King in the Garden
chapters.summary: Ansel reaches the real Aldric, buried inside his own body, who begs not for rescue but for someone to remember what he sacrificed. Ansel promises. Ansel's POV; the beat is the weight of witness.

chapters.title: Broken Bell
chapters.summary: The crowned god strikes the bell towers, killing the keepers and severing Sera's hearing. Ansel carries her wounded from the rubble as the city's prayers turn to screams. Sera's POV; the beat is loss and rage fused into resolve.

chapters.title: Excommunication
chapters.summary: Ansel formally refuses the guild's order. Stripped of rank and ledgers, he keeps only the forbidden first ledger and his oath-blade. Veyra secretly slips him the unbinding rite. Ansel's POV; the beat is freedom that feels like falling.

chapters.title: The God's Offer
chapters.summary: Through Aldric's mouth, the god offers Ansel a trade: serve as its new swordspeaker and Sera lives rich and remembered. Ansel sees the trap — service means becoming the next thing wearing a crown. Ansel's POV; the beat is temptation honestly felt.

chapters.title: What We Keep
chapters.summary: On the eve of the unbinding, Ansel and Sera spend one ordinary night — no gods, no ledgers. They admit they love each other, knowing the rite will erase him from her mind too. Sera's POV; the beat is devastating tenderness.

chapters.title: March on the Last Hearth
chapters.summary: The god, hungry now, marches the miracle-drunk faithful on the dragon to consume the final fire outright. Ansel, Sera, and the fading Veyra race ahead through burning districts. Dual POV; the beat is desperate momentum.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: At the Hearth, Ansel breaks his oath aloud and speaks the unbinding script, tearing the god from Aldric even as the words begin erasing him from the world. Veyra dies holding the ledger open. Ansel's POV, fraying at the edges; the beat is sacrifice made luminous.

chapters.title: Ash and Crown
chapters.summary: The god starves and gutters out; Aldric wakes human and weeping in the ashes, the dragon-fire steadying. But Ansel is gone — not dead, simply unwritten — and Sera stands in the crowd unable to say why she is crying. Sera's POV; the beat is hollow victory.

chapters.title: The Line in the Ledger
chapters.summary: Sorting the ruined guild archives, Sera finds one entry that survived erasure: Ansel's own hand, recording a debt owed to Sera Iln, payable in remembrance. Reading it, she holds his name against the world's forgetting. Sera's POV; the beat is grief sharpened into defiance.

chapters.title: Remembered Into Being
chapters.summary: Sera reads the ledger line aloud each night at the rebuilt ninth bell; Aldric publicly honors the unknown swordspeaker; small impossible things — a warm cup, a familiar footstep — gather around her. Ansel's fragmented POV returns in flickers; the beat is hope as an act of will.

chapters.title: When the Wolf Breaks
chapters.summary: On the anniversary, the dragon stirs fully awake and breathes fire across the Hearth — and Ansel steps out of the flame, remembered back by one stubborn keeper and a king's decree. He and Sera meet as if no time passed. Dual POV closing; the beat is love outlasting erasure, and a new ledger opened together.
